description: Framework-agnostic headless rich text editor toolkit built on ProseMirror, with native Angular, React, Vue, and Vanilla components, Notion-style block UX, and a tree-shakeable extension model. MIT licensed. Full guides and API reference at https://domternal.dev/v1.
rules: The @domternal/core package is framework-agnostic and headless. Framework wrappers are @domternal/angular, @domternal/react, @domternal/vue, and @domternal/vanilla.

Import editor primitives and built-in extensions from @domternal/core. Optional features are separate @domternal/extension-* packages: table, image, math, emoji, mention, markdown, paste-cleanup, block-controls, toc, details, code-block-lowlight.
Use StarterKit for a batteries-included schema; wire Document/Text/Paragraph and marks by hand only for a minimal headless setup.
Notion-style block UX (slash menu, drag-to-reorder, block context menu, smart paste) comes from @domternal/extension-block-controls.
Styling is opt-in via @domternal/theme (CSS custom properties) and is separate from the headless core.
JavaScript extension exports are tree-shakeable: import and register only what you use. The optional @domternal/theme package ships one complete CSS stylesheet.

Domternal Free is the current set of 18 MIT-licensed @domternal workspace packages, including extension-paste-cleanup, introduced in 1.3.0. Domternal Pro is a separate commercially licensed suite distributed through public npm with a private source repository.

The @domternal/extension-paste-cleanup package is opt-in and introduces Office HTML paste normalization in 1.3.0, with preserve/adapt formatting, bounded localized feedback, and a standalone /html helper. It is not part of StarterKit or wrapper defaults and does not import DOCX files. A historical reviewed native baseline qualifies Word 16.113.3 for Mac copied in Safari 26.5.2, Chrome 154 and Firefox 155, and Google Docs web copied in Chrome 153 on macOS, replayed through synthetic paste events. Current committed English fixtures are authored synthetic derivatives, not new native captures. Google Docs in Safari and Firefox, Word for Windows, Word on the web, LibreOffice and Collabora remain unqualified; complete Word fidelity is not claimed. Pro DOCX import is a separate, unreleased feature.

Upgrade installed @domternal/* packages together to 1.3.1; internal peer ranges remain >=1.3.0 <2.0.0, while Core's runtime PM dependency requires >=1.3.1 <2.0.0. Read the 1.3.1 fixes and the 1.3.0 migration notes: JSON loading normalizes unsupported attributes and refused links, schema validation is stricter, and transaction callbacks include appended changes. The patch restores compatibility defaults without reverting every 1.3 behavior change. Observe onContentDiagnostic, use normalizeContent for external JSON consumers, and follow the Core README before migrating a shared document with normalizeContentAttributes.

Domternal Pro runs in customer-chosen infrastructure and requires no Domternal-operated editor cloud. Current product, pricing, and licensing facts live at https://domternal.dev/pro/, https://domternal.dev/free-vs-pro/, and https://domternal.dev/license-explained/.
Full guides, per-extension API, and the changelog live at https://domternal.dev/v1.
